author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected in place: opening its correction form shows the current date and description, and a valid submission updates that same visit without adding another, then confirms on the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction form for an existing booked visit shows that visit's current date and description prefilled.
Submitting a changed description and a date later than today updates that visit in place and confirms the change on the owner's record.
A valid correction updates the same visit and adds no additional visit to the pet.
A correction with a blank description is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again.
A correction with a date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5, NG-4).
A visible entry point to the correction form on the owner detail page — the form is reachable by its address alone in this slice; a link is deferred to a possible follow-up.
notes: NG-5 narrowed 2026-08-28 to admit this correction capability while keeping cancellation out; see docs/adr/2026-08-28-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md. Reuse the existing visit form and its `visit` model attribute per the request.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction combines two patterns already in the codebase: the visit-booking flow (VisitController.processNewVisitForm) and the pet-correction flow (PetController.processUpdateForm + updatePetDetails). Both write through the Owner aggregate root via OwnerRepository.save, matching the invariant in system-design.md Contracts (Owner is the entry point; Pet and Visit are persisted only by cascade; no VisitRepository exists). The product decision is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-28-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md. Small adjustment only: a visitId-aware model method and a visit navigation helper. system-design.md updated: VisitController Contracts row (purpose + REQ-VISITEDIT-001) and the State Machine note. No new ADR — the how is the established forward-only correction pattern, not novel or hard-to-reverse.
integration_points: Add GET/POST @RequestMapping for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit alongside the existing /visits/new pair in VisitController

The single @ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit method must branch on the presence of an optional visitId path variable, mirroring PetController.findPet(petId, required=false): visitId absent -> new Visit + pet.addVisit (create path, unchanged); visitId present -> return the pet's EXISTING visit with that id and DO NOT call pet.addVisit (edit path)

POST edit handler mirrors processNewVisitForm: replicate the manual future-date check (result.rejectValue("date","typeMismatch.visitDate")), let @NotBlank on Visit.description handle the blank-description refusal, redisplay pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm on errors, else owners.save(owner) and redirect:/owners/{ownerId} with a flash message

Prefill is automatic: the form's th:object=${visit} binds the loaded visit's current date and description, and the form self-posts (no th:action) to the edit URL, so the template likely needs no change to satisfy the acceptance criteria — the existing addVisit button label is not constrained by any AC

patterns.description: updatePetDetails: load the existing child from the aggregate by id, mutate its fields in place, saveAndFlush(owner) — the canonical in-place-correction pattern to mirror for visits
findPet with @PathVariable(required=false): the exact create-vs-edit branch shape for the visitId-aware model method
Owner.getPet(Integer id): the aggregate navigation-helper precedent; add a parallel Pet.getVisit(Integer id) (or inline the lookup in loadPetWithVisit) to fetch the existing visit

risks.risk: The single guarantee to protect (AC: correcting a visit adds no additional visit): naively reusing the create model method — which unconditionally does new Visit() + pet.addVisit — on the edit route inserts a phantom second visit, because a new (id-less) instance in the cascade set is INSERTed. This is the whole reason the model method must branch and the edit path must return the pre-existing, id-bearing instance and never call addVisit.
risks.mitigation: Edit path returns the existing visit from pet.getVisits() by id; binding mutates that tracked instance in place; owners.save(owner) cascades an UPDATE (existing id), not an insert. Assert exactly-once by asserting pet visit count is unchanged in correctingAVisitShouldNotAddAnotherVisitToThePet.

risks.risk: Fail-open on unknown visitId: if the edit path cannot find the visit and silently falls back to creating one, it violates the no-extra-visit invariant.
risks.mitigation: On a visitId not found on the pet, throw IllegalArgumentException (same shape as the existing owner/pet-not-found guards in loadPetWithVisit); do not degrade a correction into a create.

risks.risk: Identifier tampering via form binding on the mutating POST.
risks.mitigation: Existing @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id","*.id") in VisitController already blocks id/nested-id binding; visitId comes only from the path variable — the existing mass-assignment control (Threat Model) carries the new route unchanged; no new trust boundary is introduced beyond the existing visit-write one.

notes: Verdict minor, not covered: needs a new route pair, a branched model method, and a visit lookup helper — not handled unchanged. Not new: no new module, persistence mechanism, or pattern; PetController.updatePetDetails is the exact template. Basis is grep/Read of the owner-package sources (IDE oracle not connected); the covering patterns resolved as memory recalled. Preserve the aggregate invariant: introduce no VisitRepository; every write stays owners.save(owner). Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records present — silent skip.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization enforced by the nested ownerId->petId->visitId lookup chain in loadPetWithVisit: pet.getVisit(visitId) iterates only the resolved pet's own visit collection, so a visitId belonging to another pet/owner is not found and the request throws. No IDOR/BOLA path.
Mass-assignment guarded: @InitBinder setAllowedFields disallows id and *.id, so the visit identity cannot be rebound from form params; bound Owner/Visit are the DB-loaded instances.
Data integrity preserved: getVisit requires !isNew() and an id match; the update mutates the loaded instance in place and save cascades an UPDATE, adding no phantom visit.
No injection sinks: JPA findById with no query-string building; description is rendered via Thymeleaf auto-escaping.
Path variables are typed and resolved through repository/collection lookups; unknown ids throw into the standard error path.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The Javadoc on loadPetWithVisit describes only the create path ('2 goals: make sure we always have fresh data / make sure Pet object always has an id'). The method now branches on visitId: when present it loads an existing visit from the pet's collection and does not call addVisit. A future reader of the comment has no indication the method does anything beyond creating a new Visit. The comment should describe both branches — create (visitId absent: new Visit, pet.addVisit) and edit (visitId present: fetch existing visit by id, no addVisit) — so the branching logic is legible without reading the body.
findings.fix: Replace the existing Javadoc with a two-branch description: (1) when visitId is absent, a new Visit is created and added to the pet (unchanged create path); (2) when visitId is present, the matching existing visit is retrieved from the pet's collection and returned without calling addVisit — binding then mutates it in place.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Two edge cases required by the PRD are not covered for the correction path. PRD § Visits edge case 1 states 'Booking a visit for a pet that does not belong to the named owner is refused' — this applies equally to correction. No test verifies (a) a GET or POST to the edit URL with a visitId that does not exist on the addressed pet is refused, and (b) a visitId that belongs to a different owner's pet is refused. Without these guards a caller can read or overwrite any visit by constructing a URL. The dispatch prompt explicitly named both gaps.

The @BeforeEach method constructs Owner, Pet, and Visit with direct new-operator calls (new Owner(), new Pet(), new Visit()). testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction requires all new tests written from 2026-07-31 onward to wrap production constructors in factory methods. These tests are new; they must use factory methods (e.g. createAnOwner(), createAPet(), createAVisit(date, description)) from the start.
findings.fix: Introduce private static factory methods createAnOwner(), createAPet(), createAVisit(LocalDate, String) in the test class and replace the three direct constructor calls in @BeforeEach and in the Visit construction block.

findings.description: TEST_OWNER_ID, TEST_PET_ID, and TEST_VISIT_ID are irrelevant to the outcomes being tested (they are routing scaffolding). testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming requires irrelevant values to carry SOME_ or ANY_ prefix, not TEST_. TEST_ is a legacy pre-2026-07-31 pattern, not the sanctioned tier-2 naming.
findings.fix: Rename to SOME_OWNER_ID, SOME_PET_ID, SOME_VISIT_ID throughout.

findings.description: The bare string literal "Corrected description" appears in both aValidCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceAndRedirect and correctingAVisitShouldNotAddAnotherVisitToThePet as an anonymous value with no declared role. testing-principles.md § Three-Tier eliminates mystery literals. Declare it as a named local constant (e.g. String CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION = "Corrected description";) at method scope or extract to a class-level SOME_ constant if truly irrelevant.
findings.fix: Introduce a named constant for the corrected description string.

findings.description: Four of the five new test methods deviate from the BDD school declared in testing-principles.md § Test Naming: the{Subject}Should{Outcome}. Only theVisitCorrectionFormShouldShowCurrentDateAndDescription follows it. The deviating names: aValidCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceAndRedirect (subject missing 'the'), correctingAVisitShouldNotAddAnotherVisitToThePet (gerund form, no 'the'), aCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheDescriptionIsBlank (subject missing 'the'), aCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheDateIsNotInTheFuture (subject missing 'the').
